title: Hera.AI
summary: Led the redesign of the Hera space mission’s AI companion, turning live spacecraft telemetry into something anyone can explore.
intro: Hera.ai is an AI companion for the European Space Agency’s Hera mission, a spacecraft now on its way to the Didymos asteroid system. Working with [Terra Mater Studios](https://www.terramater.at/) and [Impact.ai](https://www.impact.ai/), I led the redesign of its early web app: the design strategy, the user flows, a visual language aligned with the [European Space Agency](https://www.esa.int/)’s brand, and a development-ready design system. The goal was one experience that works for a curious eight-year-old and a planetary scientist alike.
body:
## Key objectives

- Make Hera feel like a character, not a bot, through her personality, tone and proactive prompts.
- Turn telemetry into something non-experts can read, with clear visualizations and 3D models.
- Work within ESA’s brand standards while giving the product a voice of its own.

## Where it started

The MVP worked, but it had no clear entry point, the chatbot’s role was unclear, and interactions were inconsistent from screen to screen. I started with a full audit of the existing app.

![Annotated screenshots of the original Hera MVP, calling out an unclear entry point, chatbot role ambiguity, a weak Hera Feed structure and inconsistent interactions](/images/hera/hera-mvp-audit.webp)

*The original MVP, annotated with what I found.*

## Who it’s for

I began with in-depth sessions with the project’s [creator](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markus_Mooslechner) and the engineers at Impact.ai, and reviewed the chatbot’s topic data. People asked most about space exploration, the asteroid mission and where the spacecraft is right now. That set the bar for every screen: scientifically accurate, but readable by anyone.

![Catering to a broad audience: a curious 8 year old, a high school student, and a NASA expert with a PhD](/images/hera/hera-broad-audience.webp)

*One product for a wide range of curiosity and expertise.*

## Simplifying the structure

The original navigation was spread across disconnected pages. I regrouped it under a single home and defined consistent interaction patterns, so every path leads from a question to an answer.

![Site map before and after the redesign: the original scattered navigation, and the simplified structure grouped under Home](/images/hera/hera-user-flow-before-after.webp)

*Site map before and after the redesign.*

## Giving Hera a voice

Hera speaks in the first person, remembers past conversations and suggests what to ask next. Her answers can open a video, an article or a live graph beside the chat, so a question about the thrusters leads straight to the data. A voice mode lets people talk to her and hear her answer.

![Hera answering a question about the thrusters with a short explainer video](/images/hera/hera-chat-video.webp)
![Hera answering a follow-up with a live telemetry graph](/images/hera/hera-chat-telemetry.webp)

*Asking about the thrusters opens a short video, and a follow-up opens a live graph, right beside the chat.*

> **Can you explain GNC mode?**
>
> “Guidance, Navigation & Control (GNC) mode is crucial in spacecraft operations. It’s all about how I navigate and control my trajectory through space…”

## Making telemetry readable

The Live view turns raw spacecraft data into labeled readings with units, color-coded instrument status and a map of Hera’s path to Didymos. A 3D model lets anyone turn the spacecraft around and inspect it up close.

![Live view with spacecraft modes, instrument status, readings and a map of Hera’s path](/images/hera/hera-live-telemetry.webp)
![Interactive 3D model of the Hera spacecraft in an exploded view](/images/hera/hera-3d-model.webp)

*The Live view and the 3D spacecraft model.*

## A visual language for ESA

I built a design system of color, type, spacing, iconography and components that sits within ESA’s brand but feels warmer and more approachable. Small animations give Hera personality without slowing anyone down.

![Hera color palette with neutral, brand, telemetry and status colors](/images/hera/hera-colors.webp)
![Hera typography: Inter for the interface and Overpass Mono for Hera’s moments](/images/hera/hera-typography.webp)

*Color and type, each with its intended use.*

![Hera components: panel buttons and states, tooltips, dropdowns, chat input and cards](/images/hera/hera-components.webp)

*Components and their states.*

## Handoff

I delivered a clickable high-fidelity prototype and a design package of specs, components and guidelines, so stakeholders could review the vision and developers could build from it directly. I also set the timelines and ran the review cycles with Terra Mater Studios and Impact.ai.

![Walkthrough of the final high-fidelity Hera screens](/images/hera/hera-final-screens.mp4)

*The final high-fidelity screens.*

## Outcome

Hera.ai went from a barebones MVP to a complete product design. I handed over a development-ready prototype, design system and guidelines. The companion itself has since been featured by [Microsoft](https://www.microsoft.com/en/customers/story/24004-terra-mater-studios-azure-ai-foundry) and [ESA](https://www.esa.int/esatv/Videos/2026/09/Meet_our_Hera_Space_Companion).
